| Figma MCP | Product and UI teams | Figma frames, components and code context | Not the job | Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and more | Write to canvas free during beta, Full seat needed | [...] Yes, Canva has an official MCP server. It's the safest pick if your team already lives in Canva and you want the agent to search, edit and export your existing Canva designs. If you want the agent to design a new flyer, menu or post from one sentence and hand back a file where every line is still editable text, use a brief-to-layout design MCP such as Krumzi. If your work lives in Figma files, use Figma's MCP. If you only need the same template filled a thousand times, use a template API like Bannerbear.

The rest of this guide shows what each one actually returns, what it costs, and the real output from a one-sentence flyer brief we ran through an MCP on 19 November 2026.

## Is there a Canva MCP? [...] ### What is a Canva MCP alternative for Claude?

It depends on the file you need. For a new flyer, menu or post that comes back as editable layers, connect Krumzi as a custom connector in Claude. For Figma files, use Figma's MCP, and for filling one template many times, use Bannerbear's MCP.

### What design tools can Claude or ChatGPT use to create graphics?

Canva, Adobe Express, Kittl and Krumzi all connect to Claude and ChatGPT, and Figma's MCP works in Claude and many coding tools. They return different things: templates you customize, generated images, Figma frames, or layouts built from your brief. Our list of the best MCP servers for marketers covers the wider stack.

results.title: Canva MCP vs Connect API: Which to Build Your Agent On
results.content:
## Which one to build against

If your Canva agent is interactive and its core job is generating or conversationally editing designs with a user present, the remote MCP is the faster route, and it is the only path to AI generation and in-place editing. If your agent runs unattended, reacts to events, needs analytics or merges, or acts across many customer accounts, build against the Connect API, since webhooks, analytics, and headless execution live only there. Most production products end up using both: the MCP for user-facing creation and the Connect API for background pipelines. Whichever surface you pick, the per-user credential problem is identical, and that is the layer that needs production-grade infrastructure.

## Talk to us, or start building [...] ### One Scalekit connector, built on Connect

Scalekit exposes a single Canva connector, built on the Connect API, shipping 48 prebuilt tools over OAuth 2.0. There is no separate Scalekit "Canva MCP" connector to choose between; the connected-account model is the same whichever Canva surface you reason about. The setup and tool list are in the Scalekit Canva connector docs.

## Comparing them where it matters for agents

The choice is not "richer vs simpler." For Canva specifically, each path holds capabilities the other cannot reach, and the auth models diverge in ways that decide production viability. Four dimensions carry the comparison.

### What your agent can actually do [...] Your agent is a user-facing design assistant where OAuth consent in a browser is natural, for example inside Claude, ChatGPT, or a chat surface you ship.
 The job is AI generation or conversational editing: draft a graphic from a prompt, then tweak copy, colors, or images in place.
 You want Canva to maintain the tool schemas and you do not need webhooks, analytics, or unattended runs.
 You are prototyping and want a working Canva agent without writing REST integration code.

### When to use the Canva Connect API

Reach for the Connect API when the agent runs on its own or needs surface the MCP does not expose.
